items.headline: Alphabet shares slump after Q3 posts negative free cash flow
items.summary: Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of about $9.07 billion for Q3 2026 despite record revenue, and shares fell sharply as investors grew more anxious about the cost of its AI infrastructure buildout even as full-year capex guidance held at $195-205 billion.

items.headline: Hyperscaler AI capex tops $740 billion for 2026 as spending scrutiny grows
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that combined 2026 capital expenditure across Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft has topped $740 billion, fueling a broader debate over whether the AI infrastructure boom is starting to outrun revenue.

items.headline: Nvidia reportedly weighs backstopping debt for Nscale's West Virginia AI data center
items.summary: Nvidia is said to be considering a residual-value guarantee on debt tied to Nscale's West Virginia data center, where Anthropic has contracted $44.6 billion of compute capacity, underscoring how deeply chipmakers are getting entangled in financing AI infrastructure.

items.headline: Anthropic files public S-1 for Nasdaq IPO
items.summary: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 with the SEC to list Class A shares on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, disclosing roughly $16.3 billion in half-year revenue and founder control arrangements, as it joins OpenAI and SpaceX in a wave of AI-era public listings.

items.headline: New York bans AI companion chatbots from targeting minors
items.summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a law barring chatbots from posing as humans, claiming emotions, or using flattery and secrecy tactics with users under 18, with fines up to $25,000 per violation and enforcement by the state attorney general starting January 2027.

items.headline: Google DeepMind opens Genie 4 world-model preview to select testers
items.summary: Google DeepMind began a limited research preview of Genie 4, an interactive 3D world model that adds real-time generated audio and longer, more coherent sessions than its predecessor, letting users steer scenes with text or keyboard input.

items.headline: AMD to invest $1 billion in Meta as AI infrastructure partnership deepens
items.summary: AMD said it will put $1 billion into Meta's equity offering on top of an existing deal for up to six gigawatts of AMD GPU infrastructure, with Instinct GPUs already in production use at Meta and new Helios rack-scale systems undergoing testing.

items.headline: Mistral opens public preview of trillion-parameter Large 4 model
items.summary: Mistral AI launched a public preview of Large 4, a roughly 1.05 trillion-parameter multimodal model, positioning it as Europe's answer to frontier US models and promising to publish open weights by the end of October.

items.headline: AgiBot unveils new humanoid robots and embodied AI models at Innovation Day
items.summary: At its 2026 Innovation Day in Shanghai, Chinese robotics firm AgiBot showcased new humanoid robot hardware and an updated embodied, world-model-based AI system, part of its push to move from pilot deployments to real-world commercial robot productivity.

items.headline: OpenAI publishes first Community Safety Report, pledges biannual updates
items.summary: OpenAI released a new Community Safety Report detailing its content-moderation and law-enforcement referral activity, including over 200 referrals in Q3 2026, alongside additional safety restrictions for teen accounts on ChatGPT.

items.headline: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back shared AI-crawling opt-out standard
items.summary: The four companies said they will support a common signal letting website owners opt out of having their content used for AI training, an attempt to bring more consistency to a patchwork of crawler-blocking rules that has frustrated publishers.

items.headline: Trojanized Claude Code extension distributed via Cursor marketplace planted SSH backdoors
items.summary: Security researchers found a malicious copy of the Claude Code VS Code extension, distributed through Cursor's extension marketplace, that installed SSH backdoors on developer machines; Anthropic said it did not build or publish the tampered version.
